chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Kareem, from Al-Hasan ibn Harun, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I ate khabees (a porridge) until I was satiated, and I am in ihram.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have finished your rituals and intend to exit from Makkah, buy dates with one dirham and give them in charity, so it will be an expiation for that, and for what entered into your ihram from what you do not know.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram, the sacred state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.خَبِيص: Khabees, a type of porridge or cooked grain dish
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Kaffarah, expiation or compensation for a religious violation
key_terms.مُحْرِم: Muhrim, one who is in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for eating food while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of expiation for unintentional or minor violations of ihram restrictions, specifically the consumption of food. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a symbolic act of charity—purchasing dates with a single dirham—to purify the pilgrim not only for the known act of eating but also for any unknown infractions incurred during the state of consecration. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and accessibility in religious obligations, ensuring that the pilgrim’s Hajj remains valid despite minor oversights.
